{{Short description|Norwegian mathematician}}
'''Magne S. Espedal''' (23 September 1942 – 25 January 2010) was a Norwegian mathematician.

He was born in [[Fjaler]] as a son of a smallholder. He [[examen artium|finished]] his secondary education in 1962 and graduated from the [[University of Oslo]] with the [[cand.real.]] degree in 1966.<ref name=hvem/>

Espedal was appointed as an [[associate professor]] at the [[University of Bergen]] in 1971 before finishing his [[dr.philos.]] degree in 1974. He was promoted to [[docent]] in 1982 and professor of [[applied mathematics]] in 1985. He was also a [[visiting scholar]] at the [[University of Wyoming]] (1985–86) and [[Texas A&M University]] (1993–94).<ref name=hvem>{{cite encyclopedia|year=1994|edition=14th|title=Espedal, Magne S.|encyclopedia=[[Hvem er hvem?]]|editor=Arntzen, Jon Gunnar|publisher=Kunnskapsforlaget|location=Oslo|page=130|language=no}}</ref> He was inducted into the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]] in 1998.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dnva.no/c26848/artikkel/vis.html?tid=26857|title=Norske medlemmer|publisher=Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters|access-date=2 September 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070715142138/http://www.dnva.no/c26848/artikkel/vis.html?tid=26857|archive-date=15 July 2007}}</ref>

As a science and education administrator, Espedal sat on the Academic College (the board) of the University of Bergen from 1989, the council of science of [[NAVF]] from 1977 to 1984 (chair from 1982–84), the council of [[NTNF]] from 1986 to 1993 (deputy chair from 1991–92),<ref name=hvem/> and the board of science and technology in the [[Research Council of Norway]] from 1993 to 1996.<ref name=obit/> He was also one of the founders of the Centre for Integrated Petroleum Research.<ref name=memo/> Espedal was a visiting scholar at the [[University of Stuttgart]] when he died in January 2010, aged 67.<ref name="obit">{{cite news|title=Professor Magne S. Espedal|type=obituary|date=5 February 2010|work=Firda|page=31|language=nn}}</ref> After his death, an [[adjunct professor]]ship at the University of Bergen was named in his honor; the first holder being [[Margot Gerritsen]].<ref name=memo>{{cite news|url=https://pahoyden.khrono.no/forste-minneprofessorat/332881|title=Første minneprofessorat|date=17 August 2011|work=På Høyden|language=no|access-date=11 September 2026}}</ref>
